mythologySignificance:
Simhachalam near Visakhapatnam is dedicated to Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha — a rare combined form. Vaishnava sthala purana of the Andhra coast narrates Narasimha’s grace and the hill’s sanctity under successive dynasties.

Pilgrimage literature treats Simhachalam Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Temple as a tirtha — a crossing where devotion to Lord Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha is believed to bear fruit more readily than in ordinary space. Accounts summarised here follow widely cited epic, Puranic, and regional mahatmya traditions; temple priests remain the guides for ritual detail.
localBeliefs:
For most of the year the deity is covered in sandal paste; Chandanotsavam reveals the form — a dramatic annual belief climax.

Coastal Andhra families treat Simhachalam as a protective Narasimha kshetra for vows and gratitude.

First-time visitors often hear several versions of the same story from pandas, taxi guides, and elderly pilgrims — a reminder that local belief is living conversation, not a single fixed text.
